title: Enterprise Telemetry & Cost Attribution Connector Playbook
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview

This playbook describes recommended configurations and operational steps for integrating Redwood Inference usage telemetry and cost-attribution with an enterprise customer's billing/observability stack. The goal is to provide consistent, auditable usage exports, per-route/customer attribution, and near-real-time alerts for cost anomalies. Target audiences: customer success engineers, solutions engineers, platform engineers at customers, and finance contacts.

Scope

- Inbound integrations supported: Redwood Usage Webhook, Billing Export (S3/BigQuery), Prometheus metrics pull via our telemetry bridge.
- Downstream systems: Customer billing system (ERP), data warehouse (BigQuery/Redshift), observability tools (Grafana/Datadog), cost controllers (FinOps).
- Not in scope: Per-model weights for internal cost modeling (handled by internal finance team).

Goals

1. Deliver line-item granularity by API key / project / route (where available).
2. Ensure exports are delivered within 5 minutes for webhooks and within 1 hour for batch billing exports.
3. Provide a mapping template for customers to reconcile Redwood usage with their invoices.

Ownership & Contacts

- CS Lead: Sofia Martinez (author) - primary contact for playbook and cutover coordination.
- Integration Owner (Redwood): Evan Clarke - handles API keys, webhook signing, and support escalations.
- Customer Success Engineer: assigned per account (add name during onboarding).
- Customer FinOps contact: required; must approve mapping and reconciliation rules.

Prerequisites (Customer)

1. Stable endpoint for webhook receiver (HTTPS) or read-access service account for cloud export (GCS/BQ/Redshift).
2. Firewall rules allowing Redwood egress IPs (see appendix) or mutual TLS where required.
3. FinOps/finance stakeholder to validate mapping table.

Architecture & Data Flow

(Plain-text diagram)
[Client apps] -> Redwood API -> Inference Runtime -> Usage Aggregator -> (a) Usage Webhook -> Customer Receiver
                                                         
                                                          -> (b) Billing Export (S3/GCS/BQ) -> Customer Data Warehouse
                                                          
                                                          -> (c) Telemetry Bridge -> Prometheus/Grafana/Datadog

Connector Options (choose one or combine)

- Usage Webhook (recommended for near-real-time): pushes event-level or aggregated records. Supports HMAC signing and retry semantics.
- Billing Export (batch; canonical): daily/hourly files in parquet/CSV to S3/GCS or native BigQuery export. Best for invoice reconciliation.
- Telemetry Bridge (metrics): Prometheus scrape or pushgateway bridge for operational metrics (latency, qps, token counts).

Schema & Mapping Guidance

Use the following canonical fields when reconciling with customer systems. The table below is a suggested mapping; customers may add columns as needed.

| Redwood Field | Type | Description | Recommended target field name |
|---------------|------|-------------|------------------------------|
| timestamp | ISO8601 string | Event time | event_time |
| customer_id | string | Redwood customer id | customer_external_id |
| project_id | string | Customer project / org identifier | project_id |
| api_key_hash | string | 8-char hashed key for PII minimization | api_key_fingerprint |
| route | string | API route/operation name (text/generate/embed) | product_route |
| model | string | Model id or variant | model_id |
| tokens_consumed | integer | Total tokens billed in event | tokens |
| prompt_tokens | integer | Prompt tokens | prompt_tokens |
| completion_tokens | integer | Completion tokens | completion_tokens |
| cost_usd | decimal | Calculated cost USD | cost_usd |
| invoice_id | string | Optional invoice reference | invoice_reference |

Implementation Steps (detailed)

1) Design workshop (1–2 hours)
   - Participants: Redwood CSE, customer FinOps, customer platform engineer, relevant product owner.
   - Deliverable: mapping spreadsheet (CSV) with sample records and reconciliation rules.

2) Choose connector and provide credentials
   - Webhook: customer provides HTTPS endpoint and signing public key (or Redwood will sign requests with HMAC).
   - Batch export: customer provides S3/GCS bucket ARN with write permissions or a BQ dataset with write access.
   - Telemetry: customer shares Prometheus scrape endpoint or sets up a remote_write receiver.

3) Test harness setup (staging)
   - Redwood will enable test mode for the specific customer and send a fixed dataset for validation.
   - Run 3 reconciliation cycles: immediate webhook, hourly batch, and daily invoice-style export.

4) Validation checklist (must pass before production)
   - All fields in mapping table present and parsable.
   - Timestamps within 2 minutes for webhook flows.
   - No more than 0.5% dropped events over a 24-hour test.
   - Cost totals within ±0.5% compared to Redwood internal billing for test window.

Example: Usage Webhook payload (trimmed)

POST /customer/usage HTTP/1.1
Host: example-customer.com
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Signature: sha256=abcdef...

{
  "timestamp": "2026-01-17T15:12:03Z",
  "customer_id": "cust_8XY12",
  "project_id": "marketing-website",
  "api_key_hash": "a1b2c3d4",
  "route": "generate.text",
  "model": "redwood-rwkv-3-small-v1",
  "prompt_tokens": 72,
  "completion_tokens": 128,
  "tokens_consumed": 200,
  "cost_usd": 0.0142
}

CLI & IAM examples

- Granting Redwood write access to a GCS bucket (customer side - example):
  gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://example-billing-export \\n    --member=serviceAccount:redwood-exporter@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \\n    --role=roles/storage.objectCreator

- Minimal IAM for BigQuery export:
  roles/bigquery.dataEditor + dataset-level grant for redwood-exporter SA.

Validation & QA tests (automated)

- End-to-end smoke test: generate 10 synthetic requests from staging and confirm they appear in the warehouse and webhook receiver within expected windows.
- Reconciliation test: run a SQL aggregation to total tokens and cost; compare against Redwood expected totals. Example query (BigQuery):
  SELECT project_id, SUM(tokens_consumed) AS tokens, SUM(cost_usd) AS cost
  FROM `redwood_customer_billing.events_20260117`
  GROUP BY project_id

Monitoring, Alerts & SLOs

- Delivery latency: median webhook delivery <= 30s, 95th <= 120s.
- Delivery success: webhook retry success rate >= 99.5% over rolling 24h.
- Export availability: daily billing export available by 03:00 UTC daily.
- Alerts to configure in customer observability:
  - Missing export file for the day (trigger at 03:30 UTC)
  - Webhook status 4xx/5xx spike > 1% over 15m
  - Cost spike: rolling 6-hour cost increases > 200% vs trailing 7-day average (auto-mute rules recommended for releases).

Rollout & Cutover Checklist

- Week -2: Mapping workshop completed and signed by customer FinOps.
- Week -1: Staging export validated (3 cycles).
- Day -1: Final configuration exported; notify stakeholders and schedule cutover window (1 hour).
- Cutover: switch production export to customer endpoint; monitor first 2 hours closely.
- Day +1: Post-cutover reconciliation and sign-off by FinOps.

Common Troubleshooting & Known Gotchas

- Duplicate events in webhook receiver: usually caused by client-side retry without idempotency keys. Solution: use api_key_hash + timestamp + event_id dedupe window (configurable).
- Timezone mismatches: ensure all systems store timestamps in UTC.
- Partial fields in batch export: older export versions may omit prompt_tokens; mapping spreadsheet must include fallback rules (e.g., set prompt_tokens=NULL and flag record).
- Large payload rejections: customers behind strict WAFs may block long POST bodies; enable chunking or increase WAF body size to >= 512KB.

Maintenance & Upgrades

- Redwood will provide a deprecation notice for schema changes at least 90 days in advance.
- Backwards compatibility policy: we guarantee 6 months of support for deprecated fields.

Security & Compliance

- PII minimization: Redwood will redact API keys and provide api_key_hash only.
- Webhook signing: HMAC-SHA256 signing available; customers must verify signature.
- Data residency: batch exports will respect customer region settings (EU/US).
- Retention: exported files are customer property; Redwood retains temporary copies for up to 7 days in case of delivery failures.

Appendix: Network & IPs

- Redwood egress ranges (for firewall allowlist): 3.34.12.0/24, 52.14.200.0/22, 34.75.100.0/23 (note: customers should reference the canonical list in /confluence/eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking/egress-ip-list).

Appendix: Sample reconciliation SQL (Postgres)

-- Aggregate daily cost per project
SELECT project_id, date_trunc('day', timestamp) AS day, SUM(cost_usd) AS total_cost 
FROM redwood_billing.events 
WHERE timestamp >= current_date - interval '7 days' 
GROUP BY project_id, day
ORDER BY day DESC;
